title: client-sync-scratch-evy-park
content:
Purpose: quick prep for weekly sync with Brightline Analytics (AE: Omar, CSM: Evelyn). Goal: surface renewal posture, align on pilot KPIs, lock next steps for proof-of-concept (PoC) and intro to Solutions Eng for Dedicated sizing.

Background/context:
- ARR: $420k ARR, contract renewal 2026-07-15 (Q3 renewal window).
- Current usage: average tokens/day ~1.2M, peak inference latency causing ~10% request retries last month after model update.
- On plan: using Hosted API (gpt-open-11b variant). Customer asked about Dedicated/GPU isolation for data controls.
- Recent: Support ticket CS-4821 opened for intermittent rate limit spikes (investigation in progress, assigned to infra).

Notes to self (tone: consultative, slightly urgent):
- Emphasize reliability improvements in last two weeks (patch notes + latency dashboard).
- Don't oversell Dedicated — frame as recommendation by usage + regulation. Present cost/latency trade-offs with real numbers.
- Ask about any procurement timelines and compliance requirements (KMS, IP restrictions).

Agenda (30 min):
1) Quick check-in (3 min) — personal, how team's going
2) Ops update (5 min) — incidents, retry patterns, what we fixed
3) Usage & cost signal (7 min) — run rate, burst patterns, cost sensitivity
4) Pilot proposal (8 min) — Dedicated PoC scope, target KPIs, timeline
5) Next steps & owners (7 min)

Key talking points / scripts:
- "We saw ~10% retry rate in late Feb tied to a burst pattern — we've deployed a change to batching and are monitoring. Have you observed customer impact?"
- "Given your peak profile and need for data isolation, a short Dedicated pilot (4–6 weeks) will surface predictable tail-latency and give us telemetry to recommend sizing. We can cap cost during pilot with pre-agreed traffic profile."
- "If compliance is the blocker, we can propose VPC + KMS integration as a follow-up; Solutions Eng will scope effort."

Risk signals to surface / questions to ask:
- Procurement/Legal timeline for new contracts? (If >60 days, try to get early MOU)
- Any internal acceptance criteria for performance? (p95 latency target?)
- Will product team require specific logging/audit fields in outputs for compliance?

Quick account health bullets (for manager):
- Customer sentiment: cautiously optimistic; primary pain = intermittent throttling and lack of capacity predictability.
- Upside: potential $150–200k expansion if pilot proves stable + new feature bundle adoption.
- Downside: churn risk if retries continue or procurement stalls.

Pilot proposal (what I'll propose):
- Duration: 4 weeks (two-week ramp, two-week steady-state)
- Scope: Dedicated small GPU pool (2x A100 equiv) + prefix cache enabled + pinned model snapshot
- KPIs: p95 latency < 350ms, retry rate < 1%, token cost change delta < +10% vs hosted during pilot
- Exit criteria: meets p95 and retry targets for 10 of 14 steady-state days OR documented procurement approval to move to Dedicated.

Asks from customer (to validate):
- Can you share preferred traffic window(s) for the pilot? (we'll need 1–2 realistic windows)
- Who signs off for procurement (title/name)?
- Any mandatory security controls for the pilot environment?

Planned asks for internal (before meeting):
- Ask Solutions Eng for quick back-of-envelope sizing (Noah) — need by Tue EOD.
- Get cost delta estimate from finance for 4-week pilot (Aisha) — need by Wed.
- Confirm recent infra tweak details with infra (ticket link) and short note on expected risk window (SRE).

Draft next steps (capture in doc during meeting):
- Owner: Evelyn — send follow-up summary + PoC one-pager within 24h. (Due: meeting +1 day -> 2026-03-11)
- Owner: Noah Kim (Solutions Eng) — provide sizing + brief runbook for pilot env. (Due: 2026-03-09)
- Owner: Aisha Patel (Finance) — pilot cost estimate and recommended billing guardrails. (Due: 2026-03-10)
- Owner: Omar (AE) — confirm procurement contact and internal timeline. (Due: 2026-03-12)
- Owner: SRE lead — update on CS-4821 mitigation and expected residual risk. (Due: 2026-03-11)

Coaching asks for manager (quick):
- Want feedback on pilot promo language (concise risk/cost framing).
- Need help nudging Solutions Eng priority if sizing takes longer than EOD Tue.

Follow-up template I'll send after meeting (copy):
- 1–2 sentence summary of decision/pilot scope
- Bullet list of owners + due dates (mirror above)
- Attach PoC one-pager + link to Confluence playbook
- Ask for procurement contact info if not provided

Open items to track in follow-up doc:
- Need SOC2/KMS checklist from security (is this required for pilot?)
- Confirm whether model variant quantization impacts latency expectations (research)
- Capture example queries / request shapes for pilot (customer to provide)

Quick links to paste into Slack during meeting:
- Confluence playbook: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CS/pages/BR-Client+Playbook
- Pilot one-pager (draft): https://docs.google.com/document/d/1PoC-draft-example
- Jira ticket for infra: JIRA-CS-4821

Mental checklist (pre-meeting):
- Bring p95/p99 dashboards, recent incident note, and a single slide showing cost vs latency trade-off.
- Print short runbook for pilot (1 page) to share if execs on call.

Random scratch notes (may delete):
- If they ask about model drift monitoring, suggest Redwood Optimize eval hook + simple prompt-set regression check (could include manual check every 3 days).
- If procurement stalls, propose a 2-week limited pilot scoped to a single feature/route to reduce legal overhead.

End.
